findings.title: USB User-mode FX holds cannot claim arrow edits
findings.why_it_matters: A performer using the supported USB/peripheral-BLE User-preset input without a central BLE link can play and hold an FX button, but the new chord never remaps it: SMC arrows fall through to page changes and keyboard arrows generate SELECT steps. smc.up describes only the central link, while the existing host queue dispatches physical note presses independently of that flag. Use the physical held bitmap and owned key_bus to admit the target, or explicitly admit peer-zero User-host ownership, while retaining the existing disconnect cleanup and context guards.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the central-BLE-only !smc.up rejection from smc_fx_held_note, retaining fx_ready/context/physical-held/key_bus guards; add a regression that sends User-mode channel-16 FX NoteOn and arrow events through smc_midi_host with no central link, plus a keyboard-arrow step against that held target.
evidence: firmware/src/app/smc_mixer.c:2274-2275 -- if (proj.set.bt & PROJ_BT_SMC_USER) smc_message(msg, sizeof msg, allow);
firmware/src/app/smc_mixer.c:330-332 -- USB or peripheral BLE User-preset input uses a separate host MIDI ring; smc_midi_host accepts it without requiring the central link.

Trace: User-mode physical NoteOn reaches smc_button -> smc_fx_try and sets held/key_bus/fx_down; host Right reaches smc_fx_arrow -> smc_fx_held_note -> !smc.up rejection, then normal smc_page_set. smc_fx_keyboard_arrow uses the same rejected selector, so arw_frame returns the ordinary SELECT detent.

residual_risks: Static review only. Host tests, compilers, target builds, framebuffer captures and native memory placement were not executed under the owner prohibition; final glyph legibility and RAM/flash fit remain external qualification work.

testing_gaps: AGENTS.md requires candidate-pinned actual visual or interaction validation before rollout and full host tests plus Elite and Pro builds before firmware integration qualification. These gates remain pending on the qualified external environment; the owner explicitly prohibits executing them in this Codex review.

residual_risks: Static review only: builds, tests, compilers, lint, and framebuffer capture were prohibited, so the new and adapted host regressions have not been executed in this review.

findings.title: Released focus leaves glyph and target labels inconsistent
findings.why_it_matters: After holding REC on strip 1, holding REC on strip 2, then releasing strip 2, the top-bar effect glyph switches back to strip 1 while the key number and footer still identify strip 2 and its effect. The next arrow edits strip 1, so the player sees conflicting destinations immediately before changing a mapping. Resolve one displayed held target for the glyph, key number and FX footer together, or move the popup focus to the remaining held button on release.
findings.suggested_fix: When the FX action popup has a remaining held FX note, use that same resolved note for the top-bar glyph, physical strip number, footer bus/effect and page. Add a hold A, hold B, release B, arrow regression that checks consistent displayed target A and only A's map changes.
evidence: Scenario: NoteOn 0 shows strip 1 / REVERB; NoteOn 1 replaces smc_ui.action=1 and strip=1 with strip 2 / DELAY. NoteOff 1 clears its hold but does not update smc_ui.action or strip. Header fallback returns note 0, yet footer and key number still read note/strip 1. smc_fx_held_note() then returns only note 0, so the arrow modifies strip 1.
smc_release() at lines 2025-2031 only extends the popup expiry if no keys remain and releases FX ownership; it never refreshes the displayed action target after a key-up.

residual_risks: Static inspection only: actual 240x240 framebuffer legibility and both model memory/flash placement require the owner-authorized qualified-box run. No build, test, compiler, lint or framebuffer capture was executed.
